Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Provides practical, platform-agnostic optimization steps for WordPress focusing heavily on perceived performance over raw scoring metrics, detailing lazy loading, explicit dimensions for CLS, AVIF conversion, local fonts, and unneeded asset removal. modules: [SPD] topics: [core web vitals, resource optimization] tier: 3 scope_hint: baseline

Topics. core web vitals / Understanding that "perceived performance" for actual users on slow connections (tested via Chrome DevTools Network throttling to "Slow 4G") is more important than chasing a perfect 100 on PageSpeed Insights. Mitigating Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) by hardcoding explicit width and height attributes directly on image elements (matching the exact rendered size) so the browser reserves layout space before the image loads. resource optimization / Configuring the image loading attribute: enforcing loading="eager" for all images above the fold (like the hero and logo) and loading="lazy" for everything below the fold. Manually converting images to AVIF or WebP via Photopea to drastically reduce file size (e.g., from 161KB to 10KB), resizing the intrinsic dimensions to 2x the rendered size to support high-density retina displays without loading original heavy files. Unloading default WordPress bloat using tools like WP Codebox (to dequeue/deregister jQuery for logged-out users on the front-end) or Asset CleanUp (to surgically unload unused WooCommerce CSS/JS on non-cart landing pages). Improving performance by serving Google Fonts locally (downloading WOFF2 files via Google Web Fonts Helper) rather than relying on external API requests. Checking compression and caching headers: looking in the Chrome Network tab for content-encoding: gzip and x-cache: hit.

Look for. The specific rule for retina image sizing: the intrinsic size should be 2x the rendered size on the page. The specific test environment for perceived performance: Chrome DevTools -> Network Tab -> Throttle to "Slow 4G" with "Disable Cache" checked. The specific CSS rule to reduce CLS: adding explicit width and height attributes to image tags that match the exact rendered size. The specific plugin to dequeue unused scripts (like WooCommerce styles) on specific pages: Asset CleanUp. The specific file format required for optimal local font loading in WordPress: WOFF2.
Skip. Promotional references to the Oxygen builder or Cloudways hosting, focusing instead on the underlying optimization principles. Broad statements about how fast WordPress can be.
